decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display that fits the firm's core display competence and uses existing production capacity, it is likely worth retaining.
The pegboard-back cardboard display is close to the established offer and adds useful merchandising flexibility for retail customers, so it should stay in the range.
A standard cardboard quarter-pallet display is a core format in this business and is likely to remain commercially relevant even in a flat market.
The eighth-pallet format broadens the firm's core in-store display offering with a compact option that retailers commonly need, so keeping it is sensible.
The wooden display pallet is less aligned with the firm's paper-based core and is the most likely candidate for portfolio simplification and resource reallocation.
A quarter-pallet display tailored to media products is narrower in application than the firm's main display formats, making it a plausible product to discontinue.
